label: Thomas Carew's poem ‘To my friend G.N. from Wrest’
more: The Cavalier poet Thomas Carew, a guest of Henry, 8th Earl of Kent, and his wife Elizabeth, wrote it at Wrest in spring 1639. It praises the plain house, the warm welcome and streams that ‘twice surround this island Mansion’, and may be the first mention of a designed garden here.

label: Classical north front added to the old house
more: Anthony, 11th Earl, and his wife Mary gave the rambling old house a classical front to disguise its irregularities, paid for largely by Mary’s inheritance when her father died in July 1671. Sources date the work 1671 (listing), 1672 (Bedfordshire Archives) or 1672 to 1676.

label: Long Water dug (early 1680s)
more: The straight canal was made by Amabel, Countess of Kent, her son Anthony, 11th Earl, and his wife Mary. English Heritage gives the early 1680s; a 2013 survey says only that it was probably there before 1685. The Pavilion at its end came in 1709–1711.

label: Henry Wynne's sundial dated 1682
more: The dial plate, signed by the London instrument maker Henry Wynne and dated 1682, stood in the garden until it was taken to Coles Park after Wrest was sold. The Ministry won it back after 1954. The plate now in the garden is a replica.

label: Old house demolished; new house built (to 1839)
more: Thomas, 2nd Earl de Grey, inherited in 1833, found a large, crumbling house of medieval origins, and chose to rebuild rather than repair. He pulled it down while building a French-style mansion 200 metres north; parts of the old house were still standing in 1838.
